    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Continuous outcome with mean 12.5 cm/s, sd=4.46, max=75.35. Moderate right skew; assess normality of residuals and consider transformation if needed.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Bounded continuous [0,1] with mean 0.38, sd=0.24. Beta regression or arcsine-sqrt transformation may be more appropriate given bounded support."

  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures structure (8 mice, 7233-10986 trials per mouse). Standard ANOVA assumes independence; mouse-level clustering requires mixed-effects models with random intercept for Mouse.",
    "Normality: QQ-plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals for each continuous variable. Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency show extreme right skew; transformation or non-parametric alternatives likely needed.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's or Bartlett's test for equal variances across paradigms. Large sample sizes (n=3323-48846 per group) provide power to detect minor violations.",
    "Variance inflation from unbalanced design: Group sizes range from 3505 (Sham) to 48846 (Combined) — ratio of ~14:1. This affects power but not validity if other assumptions hold; use Type III SS.",
    "Success (binary): Standard ANOVA assumptions fundamentally violated; distributional assumptions of GLM (logistic) must be checked via binned residuals or Hosmer-Lemeshow tests."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target (if transformed/normalized): Tukey HSD or Bonferroni-corrected pairwise t-tests among 10 comparisons; focus on Sham vs. active stimulation conditions given large mean differences (Sham: 4.68s vs. Combined: 2.56s).",
    "For Success (logistic GLM): Estimated marginal means with Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons on log-odds scale, back-transformed to probability scale. Key contrast: Sham (0.27) vs. all others (0.67-0.78).",
    "For Path Efficiency: If rank-based ANOVA used, Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction; if transformed ANOVA, Tukey HSD on transformed scale.",
    "For Average Speed: Tukey HSD, with attention to Combined (12.83) vs. Sham (10.74) and Dim Visual (11.97).",
    "For AD: Tukey HSD on appropriately transformed scale, or emmeans from beta regression; key contrast Sham (0.24) vs. Combined (0.40) and Bright Visual (0.39).",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d or partial eta-squared for ANOVA; odds ratios for logistic regression; careful interpretation given massive sample size (trivial effects may be significant)."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Strong omnibus effect of Stim Paradigm expected for all variables based on descriptive patterns, particularly the marked impairment in Sham (lowest Success: 0.27, highest Time-to-Target: 4.68s, lowest Path Efficiency: 0.31, lowest Average Speed: 10.74, lowest AD: 0.24).",
    "Combined and Bright Visual Only likely to show best performance (highest Success ~0.78-0.79, lowest Time-to-Target ~2.56-2.61s, highest Path Efficiency ~0.50, highest AD ~0.39-0.40).",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only intermediate: similar Success (~0.67-0.69), Time-to-Target (~3.05-3.14s), Path Efficiency (~0.43), suggesting unimodal stimulation less effective than multimodal or bright visual.",
    "AD pattern suggests Combined > Bright Visual > ICMS Only > Dim Visual > Sham, potentially reflecting more directed/less variable trajectories with better stimulation.",
    "Post-hoc contrasts expected to show most active conditions significantly different from Sham; differences among active conditions may be smaller and require large-N sensitivity."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs. Sham n=3505) reduces precision for Sham comparisons and affects power calculations.",
    "Repeated measures structure ignored in standard ANOVA: 8 mice contribute multiple trials, creating within-mouse correlation that inflates Type I error if not modeled (e.g., via mixed-effects models).",
    "Extreme outliers in Time-to-Target (201s) and Path Efficiency (29.8) may distort parametric analyses; robust methods or trimming warranted.",
    "No adjustment for learning effects or trial order; performance may change over sessions.",
    "Binary Success outcome analyzed via ANOVA would be invalid; logistic or mixed-effects logistic required.",
    "AD bounded on [0,1] violates ANOVA's real-line assumption; transformation or beta regression more appropriate.",
    "Large sample size (n=76655) ensures statistical significance for trivial effects; practical significance requires effect size reporting."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for Time-to-Target, Average Speed, and AD (with appropriate transformation), and generalized linear mixed-effects models (GLMM, binomial logit) for Success, all with random intercept for Mouse and fixed effect for Stim Paradigm. For Path Efficiency, consider rank-based mixed models or robust regression due to extreme skew. Follow significant omnibus effects with emmeans-based pairwise comparisons with Tukey adjustment, reporting Cohen's d or odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals."
}
